tagline.text: A public white-sand beach at Bolinao's western edge, facing sunsets over the South China Sea

children.text: Patar Beach is a public white-sand beach at the western end of Bolinao in Pangasinan, close to the Cape Bolinao Lighthouse. Golden sand, clear water and sunsets over the South China Sea are its draw, and resorts line the shore, making it a good overnight trip from Manila.

Patar Beach lies in the barangay of Patar on the Bolinao peninsula, at the far northwest of Pangasinan. A long stretch of sand facing the open sea to the west, it is best known for the scenery around sunset, and behind the beach stand accommodations ranging from simple huts to beach resorts with pools. It is about
30–40 minutes
by car from Bolinao town center, so plan it as a separate part of your itinerary from the town sights.

The sand is golden and medium-grained, not powder-fine, so the grains feel a little coarse. On the other hand, many visitors say there is little gravel or shell debris and the water is clear, which makes it comfortable for walking or sitting. In some sections, however, rocks and coral heads lie on the bottom, and because the coast faces west, waves can be strong on some days. Swim in a relatively calm stretch, such as the area in front of a resort.

Patar is a public beach that anyone can enter, although some sections can only be reached through a resort's private entrance. The usual way to enjoy it is to rent a beachfront hut (cottage) for the day and rest in its shade. To the north are large resorts such as Puerto Del Sol, and nearby are G Beach Resort and Treasures of Bolinao.
Close by stands the
Cape Bolinao Lighthouse
(about

tall, built in 1905), and other Bolinao sights such as Enchanted Cave and Bolinao Falls can be covered in a day by tricycle. That is why the most common plan is a one-night stay with Patar as your base: sights by day and the beach sunset in the evening.
Patar faces west, so the highlight is the time when the sun sinks toward the horizon. Sunset ranges between about
and
depending on the season, so it is comfortable to claim a spot around

The medium-grained golden sand runs on for a long way, which makes it good for barefoot walks. Many reviews say there is little gravel or shell debris, but rocks show in some sections, so check the bottom before you walk.

blocks.title: A day in a beachfront cottage

children.text: A beachfront hut costs around
a day depending on size and position. Some guides say you can bargain if you are fewer than five people or stay half a day, so ask the price as soon as you arrive and settle it.

blocks.title: Shallow swimming in front of resorts

children.text: The areas in front of resorts are relatively calm and good for splashing about. The water is clear enough that some visitors snorkel lightly, but the coral stones on the bottom are sharp, so be sure to bring aqua shoes.
This hilltop lighthouse near Patar stands about
tall, with its light about
above sea level. Climbing the tower is often closed off, so it is a place to enjoy by looking out over the sea from the hill.
Around Patar there is a rocky shore, good for watching waves break and for looking at tide pools. The rocky sections are not suitable for swimming, so just take photos and walk.
A tricycle charter covering Enchanted Cave, Bolinao Falls 1 and 2, the Balingasay River and more is quoted at around
for up to four people. Agree on the stops and waiting time before you set out.
Bolinao is a fishing town, so the seafood is fresh. Having grilled shrimp, squid or fish at a resort restaurant or beach stall for dinner, then carrying on with the sunset, is a popular combination.
Board a late-night bus to Bolinao at Cubao or Pasay in Manila. The trip takes about
6–7 hours
, so leaving around midnight gets you there in the early morning.
Arrive in Bolinao town, withdraw cash in advance and buy drinking water. There are almost no ATMs around Patar.
Take a tricycle to your accommodation at Patar Beach and leave your bags. The beach is quietest in the early morning.
Take in the view from the Cape Bolinao Lighthouse hill, then swim in the cave at Enchanted Cave.
Have lunch in town or at a resort restaurant, then splash about at Bolinao Falls.
Return to Patar and rent a cottage or find a spot on the beach. With the day's heat easing, it is a good time to walk.
Watch the sunset. Do not swim after dark; have a seafood dinner at a resort or beach restaurant.
A day trip is possible, but the travel alone takes more than
12 hours
round trip, so staying overnight is far more relaxed.
Have breakfast at your lodging and head to the beach.
Rent a cottage for the day, leave your things there and swim lightly in a calm stretch.
Eat lunch at a beach stall or resort restaurant. Food near the beach costs more than in town, so bring snacks and water in advance.
The midday sun is strong, so rest in the shade or take a nap.
Walk toward the rocky shore and the lighthouse.
Watch the sunset and get out of the water before the sun goes down.
Direct buses to Bolinao run from the Cubao and Pasay terminals in Manila. Five Star, Victory Liner and Solid North are among the operators mentioned, and the trip takes about
6–7 hours
Fares vary widely between sources, roughly
depending on the company and class (ordinary, air-conditioned, deluxe). Check departure times and fares at the terminal.
Get off in Bolinao town (the poblacion) and take a tricycle to Patar.
Many buses leave late at night, and leaving around midnight gets you in the early morning. First and last bus times can change, so check the latest notice.
From Manila, take NLEX and TPLEX, exit at Ramos or Paniqui, and continue through Alaminos into Bolinao. The drive is said to take about
5–6 hours
Beach parking for a car is about
, and sources differ; if you stay at a resort, you use its own parking.
From Bolinao town to Patar is about
30–40 minutes
by car.
A one-way tricycle ride is quoted at about
. The price is per vehicle, not per person.
After
tricycles are hard to find, so arrange your ride back in advance.
A full-day charter is around
for up to four people. Decide the stops first.

Patar Beach is best in the dry season, November to May. March to May in particular has clear weather and high popularity, but it is also crowded. On weekends and holidays there are many visitors, and weekday early mornings are the quietest.
During the rainy season from June to October, waves on the west-facing coast are often high, so you should avoid swimming. Sunsets are also often hidden by cloud at this time.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Most lodging is lined up along Patar Beach. Beach resorts facing the sea are around
a night, and larger resorts cost more. Simple guesthouses or huts are about

. Names that come up often are G Beach Resort, Puerto Del Sol Beach Resort, Casa Carolina Beach Resort and Rockview Sunset Beach Resort, but prices and condition change often, so check before booking. Lodging on the rocky shore has good views but may have a narrow strip of sand or hard swimming.
There are few shops and restaurants around Patar and almost no ATMs. Get cash and drinking water in Bolinao town in advance. It also helps to download a map in town beforehand.

Bolinao is a fishing town, so the seafood is fresh and fairly priced. The usual way is to pick shrimp, squid, crab or fish and ask for it grilled or fried. Prices are set by weight, so ask for the total before ordering. Some lodgings allow outside food, but the rules differ, so check first.
Keep the receipt for the Bolinao unified fee of
with you. It is often checked at other Bolinao sights, and many visitors report not paying again once paid.
Bring aqua shoes. There are rocks and coral stones on the bottom.
To see the sunset, claim your spot before
. Visitors increase in the afternoon.
Bring plenty of cash. There are almost no ATMs around Patar, and many places do not take cards.
In the peak season of March to May and on weekends, lodging fills up early. Book ahead.
Before booking beach lodging, check on the map and in reviews whether it is a sandy beach or a rocky shore.
Settle the price and time for cottages and tricycles before you use them.
Take your trash with you, and do not step on coral or take shells away.
Patar faces west, so waves and rip currents can be strong on some days. Many stretches have no lifeguards, so do not go in if the sea is rough.
Rocks and coral heads lie on the bottom, and you can hurt yourself if you enter barefoot.
Swimming after sunset and at night is not safe, so get out of the water before the sun goes down.
Waves break hard on rocky shore sections, so do not swim there and do not stand near the edge.
The midday sun is very strong. Wear a hat and sunscreen and drink water often.
Fees and rules (unified fee validity, parking, access rules) differ between sources and may change, so check the latest notice.
The town at the northwestern tip where Patar belongs, with St. James the Great Parish Church and a market. It is about
30–40 minutes
from Patar by car.
A lighthouse built in 1905, about
tall. It is close to Patar and can be reached on foot or a short ride, though entry into the tower is restricted.
Enchanted Cave offers swimming in an underground cave, and Bolinao Falls offers splashing about. Entrance fees differ by place, so confirm them locally.
An island group in Alaminos, about
1 hour
from Bolinao by bus. It is better to plan it separately than to combine it into the same day.
